title: Introducing Playtest Hub for UE-MCP: Agentic QA Automation
author: db-lyon
selftext:
PIE Studio was one of the first official ue-mcp plugins, allowing agents to author and execute deterministic playtests using your project's actual input actions.

PIE Studio has since been absorbed into the core ue-mcp toolset, and with the latest beta releases of ue-mcp and Studio, I'm introducing **Playtest Hub**, an experimental environment for managing and automating QA throughout game development.

The system is organized around three concepts:

**Playtests:** Repeatable gameplay scenarios with automated assertions and optional human validation.

**Goals:** Collections of playtests and dependent goals that collectively validate a feature or gameplay system.

**Milestones:** Collections of goals that establish measurable acceptance criteria for a development milestone.

You and your agents can now:

\- Author, manage and execute structured test plans.

\- Track playtest health against specific project revisions and test script versions.

\- Queue entire goals for automated execution when the editor is available.

\- Delegate failed playtests to agents for diagnosis, remediation and retesting.

\- Identify failing or outdated tests from a centralized dashboard.

\- Watch live gameplay during automated playtests, including remotely from your phone.

The broader objective is to give developers a way to measure development progress against actual gameplay behaviors, catch regressions, and further reduce the overall tedium of their workflows. 

Playtest Hub is currently experimental and available in the latest beta release of UE-MCP Studio, under **Settings → Experiments.**

As always, feedback is welcome.
